title_en: Li Quanzhi, Wei Duanfang, and Xie Xuezhong — case of speculation and harboring

full_text_en:
Li Quanzhi, Wei Duangfang, and Xie Xuezhong — Case of Speculation and Profiteering and Harboring

Defendant: Li Quanzhi, male, 33 years old, native of Lipaifang Village, Hugang Township, Dancheng County, Henan Province, unemployed. Arrested on October 16, 1987.

Defendant: Wei Duangfang, male, 52 years old, peasant of Weizhuang Village, Taikang County, Henan Province. Arrested on November 2, 1987.

Defendant: Xie Xuezhong, male, 28 years old, peasant of Wuzhuang Village, Chengguan Town, Dancheng County, Henan Province. Arrested on October 31, 1987.

The Baoding Branch of Hebei Provincial People's Procuratorate instituted a public prosecution with the Baoding Intermediate People's Court against defendants Li Quanzhi, Wei Duangfang, and Xie Xuezhong for the crimes of speculation and profiteering and harboring. The court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and, after a public trial, found the following facts:

During the period from spring 1984 to April 1987, defendant Li Quanzhi, together with Lü Changyou (a co-defendant who has been sentenced), planned and colluded with Zhang Chuanbo and Qian Litang (both co-defendants who have been sentenced) to counterfeit the trademark "Artificial Bezoar of the Biochemical Pharmaceutical Factory Affiliated to the Freezing Plant of Shangqiu Prefecture, Henan Province." With the participation of his elder brothers Li Quanzhong and Li Quanxiao and his wife Zhao Ping (all co-defendants who have been sentenced), and using starch, berberine hydrochloride, vitamin B2, and others as raw materials, he illegally manufactured fake artificial bezoar. Then, on the condition of paying a commission of RMB 5 for each kilogram of fake artificial bezoar sold, Li Quanzhong and Li Quanxiao repeatedly sold the fake product to Lü Changyou, Yin Junqi, Wang Lijie (Yin and Wang are both co-defendants who have been sentenced), and others. Lü Changyou, Yin Junqi, and Wang Lijie resold the purchased fake artificial bezoar at a markup in the traditional Chinese medicine market of Anguo County, Hebei Province, and after multiple transfers, it was sold to traditional Chinese medicine distribution units and pharmaceutical factories in Liaoning, Jilin, Shandong, Hebei, Shanxi, Henan, and other provinces, totaling 1,168 kg, with an aggregate business turnover of over RMB 960,000 and illegal profits of over RMB 320,000, causing direct economic losses to the state of up to RMB 3,000,000. Among them, defendant Li Quanzhi's illegal business turnover exceeded RMB 270,000 and his illegal profits exceeded RMB 200,000, seriously disrupting the management of the traditional Chinese medicine market and undermining the socialist economic order.

After the case was discovered, defendant Li Quanzhi instructed Li Quanzhong and Li Quanxiao to throw some fake artificial bezoar and bottles containing berberine hydrochloride and vitamin B2 into the Gexin River in Dancheng County, destroyed the counterfeit artificial bezoar trademark plates and the already printed fake trademarks, and thus destroyed incriminating evidence. Defendant Li Quanzhi, together with Zhao Ping, also transferred RMB 160,000 in illegal proceeds to the home of his nephew Zhao Guozhi (a co-defendant, already sentenced) for concealment. Thereafter, Li Quanzhi absconded to Anhui, Shanghai, Taikang County, Henan Province, and elsewhere, and instructed co-defendant Wei Duangfang to send a letter to Xi'an to the public security organs in an attempt to divert the investigation.

Defendant Wei Duangfang and Zhang Jinshan (at large), knowing that defendant Li Quanzhi was a criminal, repeatedly provided him with shelter from May to September 1987. Wei Duangfang received RMB 880 in illegal proceeds.

Defendant Xie Xuezhong, under the instruction of defendant Li Quanzhi, on the night of mid-June 1987, together with Zhang Jinshan, dug up the illegal proceeds from the yard of Zhao Guozhi's home; the following night, defendant Xie Xuezhong drove a car to transport defendant Li Quanzhi and the illegal proceeds to the highway of Laozhong Township, Huaiyang County, assisting Li Quanzhi in continuing his escape. Xie Xuezhong received RMB 3,000 in illegal proceeds.

The above criminal facts are confirmed by the tools used for the crime, the stolen goods, the recovered illegal proceeds, certificates from drug inspection and health administrative departments, witness testimony, and the confessions of co-defendants. The three defendants all confessed without reservation. The evidence is reliable, sufficient, and conclusive.

The Baoding Intermediate People's Court, after trial, held that: Defendant Li Quanzhi and the 16 defendants, including Li Quanzhong and Li Quanxiao, who were sentenced by the Anguo County People's Court on October 9, 1987, for the crimes of speculation and profiteering, harboring stolen goods, and harboring, belonged to the same case, and Li Quanzhi was the principal offender. At that time, because Li Quanzhi was at large, it was not possible to try the case together. Defendant Li Quanzhi, with the purpose of seeking exorbitant profits, violated industrial and commercial management regulations, operated without a business license, illegally manufactured and resold fake artificial bezoar, seriously disrupting the market management of traditional Chinese medicine and undermining the socialist economic order. His conduct constituted the crime of speculation and profiteering as stipulated in Article 118 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. Li Quanzhi's illegal business turnover and illegal profits were both particularly huge, and the circumstances were particularly serious. According to Item (1) of Article 1 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Regarding the Severe Punishment of Criminals Who Seriously Sabotage the Economy, he should be severely punished. Defendant Wei Duangfang, knowing that defendant Li Quanzhi was a criminal, harbored him; defendant Xie Xuezhong, knowing that the huge sum of money buried at Zhao Guozhi's home was proceeds from defendant Li Quanzhi's crime, withdrew and transferred it, and used a car to assist Li Quanzhi in continuing his escape. Their conduct constituted the crime of harboring as stipulated in paragraph 2 of Article 162 of the Criminal Law. In accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law, the illegal gains of Li Quanzhi, Wei Duangfang, and Xie Xuezhong and the personal property used for the crime shall be recovered and confiscated. Accordingly, on May 13, 1988, the Baoding Intermediate People's Court sentenced Li Quanzhi to death for the crime of speculation and profiteering, and in accordance with paragraph 1 of Article 53 of the Criminal Law, deprived him of political rights for life, and ordered the recovery of RMB 140,400 in illegal proceeds; for the crime of harboring, sentenced Wei Duangfang to six years' imprisonment with recovery of RMB 880 in illegal proceeds; sentenced Xie Xuezhong to three years' imprisonment with recovery of RMB 3,000 in illegal proceeds, and confiscated one Nanjing GAZ-brand automobile.

After the judgment was pronounced, Li Quanzhi and Wei Duangfang were dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment and appealed respectively to the Hebei High People's Court.

After trial, the Hebei High People's Court held that: Appellant Li Quanzhi counterfeited another's registered trademark, illegally manufactured and resold fake artificial bezoar. His conduct constituted the crime of speculation and profiteering, and his illegal business turnover and illegal profits were both particularly huge, the circumstances were particularly serious, and he should be severely punished. Li Quanzhi appealed arguing that the manufacture of fake artificial bezoar was done in partnership with others. Upon investigation, the already-sentenced co-defendants Li Quanzhong and Li Quanxiao and others, only with the purpose of obtaining a reward of RMB 0.1 per kilogram of raw material processed for fake artificial bezoar, participated in processing the raw materials for Li Quanzhi's fake artificial bezoar on several occasions, and also participated in bagging and reselling. They were not partners in manufacture. Li Quanzhi's wife Zhao Ping also denied that Lü Changyou, Li Quanzhong, and Li Quanxiao were in partnership with Li Quanzhi. Therefore, Li Quanzhi's appeal was clearly an attempt to shift blame. Appellant Wei Duangfang harbored Li Quanzhi in his home for over 40 days, sent a letter for Li Quanzhi to Xi'an to divert the investigation, and kept huge sums of illegal proceeds for Li Quanzhi. These were serious circumstances, and there were no statutory mitigating conditions. His grounds for appeal could not be established. Accordingly, in accordance with Item (1) of Article 136 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the court ruled on November 10, 1988, to dismiss the appeals of Li Quanzhi and Wei Duangfang and affirm the original judgment. And in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 145 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the ruling affirming the first-instance judgment sentencing Li Quanzhi to death and depriving him of political rights for life was reported to the Supreme People's Court for approval.

The Supreme People's Court, in accordance with the death penalty review procedure provided by the Criminal Procedure Law, reviewed the case. It held that: The facts of defendant Li Quanzhi's crime as determined by the original trial were clear, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, the conviction was accurate, the punishment was appropriate, and the trial procedure was lawful. By decision of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, on December 21, 1988, the court approved the criminal ruling of the Hebei High People's Court affirming the original judgment sentencing Li Quanzhi to death and depriving him of political rights for life for the crime of speculation and profiteering.
